hero.title: Transfer files from phone to PC
hero.body: Cables are fiddly and cloud uploads are slow. BIShare moves photos, videos, and files straight from your iPhone or Android to any Windows, Mac, or Linux computer — wirelessly over your local Wi-Fi, or with a link the PC opens in any browser. No cable, no cloud round-trip.

why.title: Why getting files off your phone is such a hassle
why.body: Plug an iPhone into a Windows PC and you only see the camera roll — often after it asks for iTunes. Android over USB likes to drop mid-copy. Emailing yourself hits a 25 MB limit and re-compresses your photos. Cloud apps make you upload everything, then download it all again on the other side. BIShare skips the lot: your files go straight from phone to computer, at full quality, over the network you're already on.

how.title: Two ways to get files onto your computer

0.b: Pick your computer in BIShare and the files fly straight across, end-to-end encrypted — nothing is stored on a server. It even works over your phone's hotspot when there's no internet at all.

1.b: BIShare hands you a link, a QR code, and a 6-character code. Open the link in any browser on the computer and download — no app, no account. The link auto-expires after 24 hours.

2.b: iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux — one app, every direction. Push files from your phone to your PC, or send from the PC back to any phone.

faq.title: Transferring files from phone to PC: FAQ

0.q: How do I transfer files from my phone to my PC wirelessly?
0.a: Install BIShare on your phone. On the same Wi-Fi, open it, pick your computer, and send — the files transfer directly, end-to-end encrypted. If you're not near the PC, share the link BIShare gives you and open it in the computer's browser to download. No cable required either way.

1.q: How do I transfer photos from iPhone to a Windows PC without iTunes?
1.a: Send them with BIShare instead of plugging in. Over Wi-Fi it copies your photos straight to the PC at full resolution — no iTunes, no "Trust This Computer" dialog, and no 25 MB email limit. HEIC photos come across as-is, and you can grab videos and any other file the same way.

2.q: Can I move files from Android to a Mac or Linux computer?
2.a: Yes. BIShare treats every platform the same, so Android → Mac and Android → Linux work exactly like Android → Windows. On the same network it's a direct transfer; otherwise use the share link, which opens in any browser on macOS or Linux.

3.q: Is there a size limit when sending files from phone to PC?
3.a: Nearby transfers over your own Wi-Fi have no size cap — send multi-gigabyte videos if you like. Share links carry files up to 10 GB for free, and the link expires automatically after 24 hours.

4.q: Do I need to install anything on the computer?
4.a: Not to receive by link — any browser works, with no app or account. For fast, direct nearby transfers, install the free BIShare app on the computer too; it unlocks two-way sending and higher speeds, but it's never required just to download a shared file.
